narrative:
The model estimated a 35% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. Although that does not mean default is certain, it was above the bank’s approval cutoff, so your application was denied.

The strongest influence was the requested loan duration. Your nine-month term is much shorter than the approved average of about 19 months, so this pushed toward good credit. The second most important factor was your checking account being overdrawn below zero DM. Only about 12.6% of approved applicants had this, making it a strong warning sign that pushed toward bad credit. The third factor was your occupation in management, self-employment, or a highly skilled role, which pushed toward good credit by suggesting steadier income. The model still rated you as a bad risk because the overdrawn account, combined with other risk signals, outweighed the favorable short duration and job.

To improve your chances next time, bring your checking account out of overdraft and keep it positive for several months. Build savings beyond the lowest range and consider adding a co-applicant or guarantor. You may also ask the bank what specific cutoff applied and whether extra proof of stable income or a manual review is possible.
